'''Catherine Doléans-Dade''' (24 January 1942 – 19 September 2004) was a [[French American]] [[mathematician]]. She made significant contributions to the calculus of [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingale]]s, including a general change of variables formula, a theorem on [[stochastic differential equation]]s, and exponential processes of semimartingales.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://withits.epfl.ch/_media/events/slides-hajek.pdf|title=A great probabilist: Catherine Doléans-Dade|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703055305/http://withits.epfl.ch/_media/events/slides-hajek.pdf|archive-date=2022-07-03|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After earning her doctorate from the [[University of Strasbourg]] in 1970, she became a professor in the Mathematics Department of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]]. She died of cancer in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.illinois.edu/People/memoriam_doleans-dade.html|title=In Memoriam: Catherine Doleans-Dade, Mathematics - Illinois|work=University of Illinois|access-date=2015-04-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150209175112/http://www.math.illinois.edu/People/memoriam_doleans-dade.html|archive-date=2015-02-09|url-status=dead}}</ref>
